correctness.rationale: The exact product DP^{b_n}...DP^{b_1} reduces to a diagonal multiplier 2^{(n±S)/2} times P^t, where S sums suffix-parity signs. Even-parity words are in bijection with all n-1 free suffix signs; excluding the single all-left word yields every binomial cell. The maximum admissible |S| is n-2 and the folded-normal limit is the classical i.i.d. sign CLT. The originating paper proves the required word-to-periodic-point bijection. Full exact rational checker verified all 2^n-1 nontrivial words at each n=1,...,11, including branches and boundaries. The derivation, not finite tests, covers unbounded n.

value.rationale: The founding paper explicitly emphasizes nonuniform periodic expansion. The exact finite-n law and folded-normal asymptotic identify the entire prevalence of multiplier anisotropy, exhibiting a sharp dichotomy between a worst-case rate 2^(1/n) approaching 1 and a typical rate approaching sqrt(2) with order-n^(-1/2) fluctuations. The law supplies a natural intrinsic periodic-point statistic unavailable from real/nonreal totals, rather than arbitrary data or a routine restatement.
